note: Built as ballot/lean/mn_endorsements.json is. Each record is one line of one party page, matched to one race and one candidate on the official lists already loaded in ballot_local_2026.sqlite (office, place and name all fit, one fit only). Ohio differs from Minnesota: its parties nominate in the May 5 partisan primary, judges included, and for November most of them publish a slate card or a list of their candidates rather than endorsements. Only a page that itself says 'endorsed' is under endorsements. A slate card, an 'official slate' or a party's 'sample ballot' that does not say endorsed is under other_support with the page's own word in 'kind', kept apart and not for showing as an endorsement; the Ohio Republican Party's 88 county slate cards are there (each record's address is the county's PDF; 'lists' names the page that links them once). A bare list of a party's candidates is not collected at all (see not_read). This matters most for judges of the Court of Common Pleas, who are nominated by party and printed without one in November. 'election' appears only when the candidate is on a primary list and not on the November list (legislative districts whose November list is not loaded). Governor and lieutenant governor are one November ticket, so a page's two lines are one record. Federal offices and party offices on these pages are outside this file. The same candidate stands on several lists: count once per party. Two lists (Franklin County and Lucas County Democrats) are published as pictures: they were read by eye, and a second reader read both pictures again without the first reading and confirmed every record (33 Franklin, 9 Lucas; 2026-10-02). The Lucas list's older address now redirects to the party's home page; its page at the address recorded here carries the same list as text under the heading 2026 Endorsements. Every page in 'lists' was opened again when this file was built and a record is kept only if the page, or the PDF, still showed the name; pages were fetched with the kit's honest User-Agent after checking each site's robots.txt, and a site that forbids programs, shows a CAPTCHA or refuses the program was not opened (see not_read). Only 23 of Ohio's 88 counties have county and court races loaded and many legislative districts have no November list yet, so lines for other places cannot match yet; they are listed under the two 'unmatched_listed' keys with the reason.
